prompt_en: A medical-horror photograph built around a moment of biomedical unease. Portray a fictional person using the supplied reference image, preserving facial proportions and the short dark bob with wispy fringe. She appears as a laboratory researcher at a stainless-steel counter in a small cryobank room after midnight. An open freezer behind her reveals orderly racks coated in white frost. She has slid one metal vial rack onto the counter and stopped. A single transparent sealed ampoule stands in its front row between two visibly frosted ampoules. Through the clear glass, a pale folded tissue culture sits entirely within amber liquid, with a level meniscus and a small air space below the cap. Distinct condensation droplets gather beneath the sealed cap and a fresh wet circle surrounds the ampoule's base on the steel, while neighboring vials remain matte with frost. The low open rails of the rack leave the clear vial's body and wet base visible. Her left gloved hand braces the rack's near edge while her right gloved hand hovers just above the anomalous ampoule, fingertips paused before contact, a small air gap visible between fingers and cap. The tray rests fully on the counter; her wrists and forearms lead clearly back to her seated body. Her attention stays on the specimen, brows subtly tightened, lips gently parted as she weighs the unexplained change. An unbuttoned white laboratory coat falls over a charcoal tank, its ordinary softness and the quiet light on her cheek lending a subtle intimate human presence against the cold apparatus. On the right side of the same laboratory bench, a compact microscope stands beside a rack of glass slides with small paper end labels; the sealed specimen ampoule is a separate container in front of them. Frame from her waist to above her head with the specimen rack prominent in the lower foreground, her three-quarter face on the left and the open freezer receding on the right. The camera looks slightly down from chest height across the counter, keeping the clear ampoule large enough to distinguish its liquid surface from the glass. A cool task lamp grazes the vial glass and damp steel, while a dim warm corridor light catches her cheek and the edge of her hair. Moderate depth of field keeps her face, hovering fingers and thawed vial readable together, with the microscope and labeled slide rack still identifiable. Real photographic skin, fine flyaway hair, matte frost and condensed water; restrained clinical color, a still, unresolved inspection.
